items.claim: 5:1-5:4 is one movement (feast, vessels, praise of the idols) and both its edges fall where the form says; but the row lists the chapter line among its onset signals, and it calls the unit before the seam a decree although the verse before the seam (web:Dan.4.37 = oshb:Dan.4.34) is first-person praise.
items.both_sides: Onset 4:37/5:1: close side is the king's first-person praise at web:Dan.4.37 = oshb:Dan.4.34 with a PE after it (one witness); onset side is the subject-first royal clause at 5:1 (king named first, then the verb, then the feast), a new king and a new setting. Close 5:4/5:5: close side is the praise of the gods at 5:4 (praise_aram) completing the drinking; onset side is the time formula at 5:5 (at_that_moment_aram) with a new agent, the hand. No mark after 5:4. Both edges are two-sided in the text.

suggested_fix.fact: the onset signal at 5:1 is the subject-first royal clause that names the new king before the verb; a chapter line is not a signal and is removed from the signal list; the verse before the seam is first-person praise, not a decree

evidence: FINDING 1 (gravest): observed_substrate_signals[0] reads 'new chapter and new king at 5:1 (WEB text)' and boundary_rationale opens 'the chapter opens on a new king'; the book's evidence rule is that chapter divisions never drive or corroborate a boundary.

FINDING 2: boundary_rationale says the PE 'closes the preceding decree (web:Dan.4.37 = oshb:Dan.4.34)' and in the same sentence that the far side is 'Nebuchadnezzar's first-person praise'; Dan_web_clean.txt 4:37 is praise in the first person, and the neighbouring row over 4:34-4:37 is typed doxology_or_prayer.
FINDING 3 (minor): '(EXTRACTED OSHB mark layer and WEB text)' stands beside 'the onset seam is two-sided'; the PE and the praise are in those layers, the two-sidedness is a weighing.

items.claim: 5:5-5:9 is one scene: the hand writes (5:5), the king is shaken (5:6), he summons and offers the reward (5:7), the wise men fail (5:8), and the king is shaken again and more (5:9). The fear of 5:6 returns at 5:9 and frames the scene, which the row does not cite but which strengthens its close.
items.both_sides: Onset 5:4/5:5: see W3-001, two-sided. Close 5:9/5:10: close side, 5:9 repeats the changed face of 5:6 with the lords now perplexed, a rounded ending; onset side, 5:10 opens subject-first on a new character, the queen, who enters and speaks with the court greeting (o_king_live_forever_aram). No mark after 5:9. The SAMEKH after 5:7 stands inside the scene, between the summons and its failure.
evidence: CHECKED pmarks_Dan.json (WLC/OSHB, single witness, MT face; identity with WEB in chapter 5): SAMEKH after Dan.5.7 present and named as SAMEKH; no mark after 5:5, 5:6, 5:8 or 5:9; K/Q entries Dan.5.5 x1, Dan.5.7 x2, Dan.5.8 x2 and none at 5:6 or 5:9; paseq at Dan.5.7; notes n=1 at Dan.5.6 and n=k at Dan.5.7. Every count in the row matches, and nothing in the span is undisclosed.

CHECKED Dan_oshb.txt Dan.5.5: the two-word Aramaic quotation is an exact substring at the start of the verse. Dan.5.6 and Dan.5.9 both carry the face-changed clause (read in the Aramaic and in WEB 5:6, 5:9).

FORM: cutting at the SAMEKH would part the summons (5:7) from its outcome (5:8); the row rejects that rival for the right reason. Confidence medium is honest: the close has no mark but is two-sided in the text.
NOTE (not a defect of the seam): the row names the tag 'answered_and_said' without saying which of the inventory's two readings it means; here both readings hold 5:7, so nothing false is asserted.

items.claim: 5:13-5:16 is a coherent unit, the king's address to Daniel ending on the offer, and both edges are sound; but the rival the row weighs (an onset at 5:14) is not the strongest one. The stronger rival puts the close one verse later, after 5:17, so that the king's offer and Daniel's answer to it stand together and the recital opens at 5:18.
items.both_sides: For the row's close at 5:16/5:17: the king's speech ends at 5:16, a PE follows (one witness), and 5:17 opens with a full speech frame (then_aram plus the strict answered-and-said frame) and a new speaker. For the rival close at 5:17/5:18: 5:17 answers 5:16 point for point (the gifts refused, the reading promised), so it completes the exchange; 5:18 opens with direct address to the king and begins the recital of his father's reign, a new speech function. Against the rival: no speaker change and no mark at 5:17/5:18, and 5:18 has no frame of its own. The row's cut is the better grounded; the rival is the one worth recording.

suggested_fix.fact: the strongest rival is a close after 5:17, joining Daniel's refusal of the gifts to the offer it answers and opening the recital at the direct address of 5:18; it is declined because the speaker changes at 5:17 with a full speech frame and a PE (one witness) follows 5:16, while 5:17/5:18 has neither

items.claim: 5:17-5:24 holds one movement (refusal, recital of the father's humbling, charge against the son, the hand sent) and medium_low is the honest grade for its close inside one speech; but device_notes sets EXTRACTED beside a reading (that the formulas recall the father's humbling), and strongest_rejected_alternative carries a count and a weighing with no tier word.
items.both_sides: Onset 5:16/5:17: two-sided, see W3-004. Close 5:24/5:25: close side, 5:24 opens with then_aram (weak alone) and its 'from before him' depends on the God named at the end of 5:23, so it leans back on the charge; onset side, 5:25 presents the writing and 5:26 carries the interpretation formula. But 5:24 ends on the writing being inscribed and 5:25 takes up those very words (read in Dan_oshb.txt Dan.5.24 and Dan.5.25), so the two verses are also chained forward. Same speaker, no mark. 5:24 is a hinge verse; an edge at 5:23/5:24 is a second live rival beside the whole-speech one.

suggested_fix.fact: the inventory holds the presence of most_high_aram at 5:18 and 5:21 and of the recognition refrain at 5:21 (EXTRACTED); that they recall the father's humbling, and that the praise of 5:23 inverts 5:4, are readings (INFERRED); the rejected rival's 12 verses is a count and its 'distinct speech functions' a weighing, each owing a tier; 5:24 is a hinge whose last clause is taken up by 5:25

items.claim: 5:25-5:28 is a coherent unit of the right type (the writing presented, then glossed word by word under the interpretation formula at 5:26), but its grade is rounded up: its onset edge at 5:24/5:25 is the same edge the neighbouring row grades medium_low, it has no mark, no change of speaker, and 5:25 takes up the closing words of 5:24.
items.both_sides: Onset 5:24/5:25: close side, 5:24 ends the charge by naming the hand and the writing; onset side, 5:25 opens with a conjunction and repeats the words for the writing being inscribed from the end of 5:24, then lists the words; the interpretation formula comes only at 5:26. One speaker throughout, no mark. The evidence for an onset at 5:25 is a change of speech function alone, and the catchword pulls the other way. Close 5:28/5:29: close side, the third gloss ends the speech; onset side, 5:29 opens with then_aram and narrated action by the king. That edge is two-sided, without a mark.

suggested_fix.fact: the onset at 5:25 rests on a shift of speech function only, inside one speech, with no mark, and 5:25 repeats the closing words of 5:24; a seam with evidence of that kind is graded medium_low, the grade the adjoining row already gives the same edge

evidence: FINDING 1 (gravest): the row's own rationale says 'Same speaker across the onset seam, so the onset rests on a genre shift; medium', while the row over 5:17-5:24 says of the same edge 'a topic shift inside one speech with no mark; graded medium-low'. One edge carries two grades. The book's grading rule sends a seam with one-sided evidence to low or medium_low and forbids rounding up.

The row does not weigh this link, and its rejected rival (an onset at 5:26) is weaker than the rival that draws 5:24 forward.

items.claim: 5:29-5:30 is a sound closing unit (the promised reward given, then the king's death in that night) and its close is the parent seam, two-sided; but strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes carry claims with no tier word.
items.both_sides: Onset 5:28/5:29: close side, Daniel's speech ends with the third gloss; onset side, 5:29 opens with then_aram (weak alone) and returns to narrated action, the king's command. Two-sided, no mark. Close 5:30 / web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1: close side, the in_that_night_aram formula (its only verse in the book) and the death that fulfils the reading, with a PE after 5:30 (one witness); onset side, the succession notice names a new king. The live rival at this edge, that the succession notice closes the tale as the fulfilment of 5:28, is a parent-level question the row cannot propose; the next row records it.

suggested_fix.fact: that the reward completes the arc the death notice seals is a reading and takes INFERRED; the K/Q presence at 5:29 and 5:30 is held by the K/Q layer of the single witness and takes EXTRACTED with that layer named
